row.reason_if_0: Different business model: regulated T&D utility earning rate-based fees from retail customers vs. upstream gas producer selling commodities and wholesale power at market prices to marketers and the grid.
row.reason: Con Edison is a regulated electric, gas and steam delivery utility that serves retail end customers in New York. BKV is an upstream natural gas and NGL producer. It also has midstream, gas-fired power generation and carbon capture lines, and it sells commodities and power at market prices. The two share an energy label and some overlap in natural gas and electricity. They sit at different points in the value chain. Con Edison earns regulated rates on its networks. BKV earns market-priced commodity sales. BKV's buyers are marketers and processors, with data-center power as a growth area. Con Edison's customers are residential, commercial and government customers. BKV would be closer to a supplier to utilities than a peer.

T:P2.3.text: Con Edison's principal business segments are Consolidated Edison Company of New York, a regulated electric, gas, and steam utility; Orange & Rockland Utilities (O&R), a regulated electric and gas utility; and Con Edison Transmission, Inc.

T:P2.4.text: Con Edison of New York provides electric service to multiple million customers and gas service to multiple million customers in New York City and Westchester County. The company also provides steam service in parts of Manhattan. Visit Con Edison’s website.

T:P2.5.text: Orange & Rockland provides electric service to multiple customers in southeastern New York and adjacent areas of northern New Jersey and gas service to multiple customers in southeastern New York. Visit Orange & Rockland’s website.

T:P2.6.text: Con Edison Transmission invests in electric and natural gas transmission projects that offer customers access to diverse, low-cost energy supplies. Visit Con Edison Transmission’s website.
